pr.body:
Changes:
- Initializes unified storage when the `ResourceServer` is created, instead of doing it inside the first gRPC call it receives. This was causing context cancelled errors since the index takes too long to build within the context of the gRPC call.
- Fixes trace propagation by passing span contexts down.
- Improves index build speed using finer grain locking when writing the index cache. We were locking the whole `BuildIndex` function, which was slowing things down when building many namespaces with high concurrency.

Notes for reviewer:
- Does anything else depend on initializing US lazily? What could this break?
pr.title: Unified Storage: Init at startup, fix traces, and speed up indexing

raw_findings.body: Requests that were previously short-circuited with the stop error now bypass the initErr check entirely and proceed against a cancelled/stopped backend, producing inconsistent errors or operating on shutdown-time state instead of a clean rejection.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Runtime behavior change: shutdown no longer fences off in-flight/late requests.
raw_findings.impact: Requests that were previously short-circuited with the stop error now bypass the initErr check entirely and proceed against a cancelled/stopped backend, producing inconsistent errors or operating on shutdown-time state instead of a clean rejection.
raw_findings.root_cause: The per-request s.Init(ctx) calls were the only place that surfaced the stop-state initErr to callers; deleting them removed that guard while Stop() still relies on mutating initErr.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: If graceful post-Stop rejection is still required, keep a lightweight guard (e.g. check s.initErr / a stopped flag) at the top of the request handlers instead of removing the check outright.
raw_findings.title: Removing Init() guards disables post-Stop request rejection
raw_findings.trigger: A Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search request arrives after Stop() has been called (which sets s.initErr to "service is stopping"/"service is stopped" and cancels s.ctx).

raw_findings.body: Concurrent map read (TotalDocs) and map write (BuildIndex) can trigger Go's fatal "concurrent map read and map write" runtime panic during startup.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Intermittent runtime panic under concurrent indexing.
raw_findings.impact: Concurrent map read (TotalDocs) and map write (BuildIndex) can trigger Go's fatal "concurrent map read and map write" runtime panic during startup.
raw_findings.root_cause: Adding a TotalDocs() invocation after the watch goroutine is started introduces an unsynchronized read of the cache map that BuildIndex mutates under lock.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Have TotalDocs() acquire b.cacheMu.RLock() while iterating the cache (and/or gate this log call), so the new read site is safe against the now finer-grained BuildIndex write lock.
raw_findings.title: New TotalDocs() call reads cache map concurrently with watcher-driven BuildIndex writes
raw_findings.trigger: A write event arrives on the watch channel started earlier in init() (line 207) and triggers handleEvent -> build -> BuildIndex, which now writes b.cache under cacheMu, while this new log line invokes TotalDocs() which iterates b.cache without taking cacheMu.

finding.body: Requests that were previously short-circuited with the stop error now bypass the initErr check entirely and proceed against a cancelled/stopped backend, producing inconsistent errors or operating on shutdown-time state instead of a clean rejection.
finding.failure_mode: Runtime behavior change: shutdown no longer fences off in-flight/late requests.
finding.impact: Requests that were previously short-circuited with the stop error now bypass the initErr check entirely and proceed against a cancelled/stopped backend, producing inconsistent errors or operating on shutdown-time state instead of a clean rejection.

finding.title: Removing Init() guards disables post-Stop request rejection
finding.trigger: A Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search request arrives after Stop() has been called (which sets s.initErr to "service is stopping"/"service is stopped" and cancels s.ctx).
finding.verifier_reason: The patch removes per-request Init() calls, but the repository context shows Init() is now called eagerly at server construction time (line 258 in server.go). The Stop() mechanism sets initErr but the sync.Once in Init() means initErr is only checked once during startup, not per-request. The claim that requests were 'short-circuited' by initErr after Stop() is incorrect - Init() uses sync.Once so subsequent calls just return the cached initErr from first init, not from Stop(). The removal is intentional as init is now eager.

finding.title: New TotalDocs() call reads cache map concurrently with watcher-driven BuildIndex writes
finding.trigger: A write event arrives on the watch channel started earlier in init() (line 207) and triggers handleEvent -> build -> BuildIndex, which now writes b.cache under cacheMu, while this new log line invokes TotalDocs() which iterates b.cache without taking cacheMu.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim is that TotalDocs() reads b.cache without locking while BuildIndex writes it. However, examining bleve.go lines 137-153, BuildIndex acquires cacheMu.Lock() only when writing to b.cache (lines 137-139), and TotalDocs() iterates b.cache without locking (lines 144-153). But this is pre-existing code - the patch only adds a log line calling TotalDocs(). The race condition, if real, existed before this patch. Additionally, the watcher goroutine calls handleEvent which calls build(), but build() is in searchSupport not bleveBackend, and the actual cache write happens under lock in BuildIndex.
